title: Common DVR criterion for generation of a fraction field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A,B\subseteq K$ be unital subrings, each with fraction field $K$. Assume that $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension exactly one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\mu:A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B\to K$ be the homomorphism sending $a\otimes b$ to $ab$ (tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]). Then $\mu$ is not surjective if and only if there exists a discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O\subseteq K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$, containing both $A$ and $B$.

source.place: Tag 09N0 (varieties-lemma-glue-separated), in Situation 09MY (varieties-situation-glue); used in Tag 09NJ, proof, first paragraph.

proof.text: Let $C=\operatorname{im}(\mu)\subseteq K$. By the tensor-product construction, its elements are exactly finite sums $\sum_i a_i b_i$ with $a_i\in A$, $b_i\in B$ (integer coefficients can be absorbed in $a_i$). These sums form a unital subring: multiply two sums by distributing and use closure of $A$ and $B$ under products. Since $a=\mu(a\otimes1)$ and $b=\mu(1\otimes b)$, we have $A,B\subseteq C$. Suppose $\mu$ is not surjective, so $C\ne K$. If $C$ were a field, every $a/b\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ would belong to $C$, since $a,b\in A\subseteq C$ and $b\ne0$. Thus $C$ is a domain that is not a field.

Choose $0\ne c\in C$ which is not a unit. The principal ideal $(c)$ is proper: $1=dc$ would make $c$ a unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] with $R=C$ and $I=(c)$ to obtain a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $c$. In particular $\mathfrak m\ne(0)$.

Form $D=C_{\mathfrak m}$ using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It is the local subring $\{r/s\in K:r\in C,\ s\in C\setminus\mathfrak m\}$; equality of such fractions is checked by cross multiplication in the field, so this realizes the localization injectively in $K$. Its maximal ideal consists of fractions whose numerator lies in $\mathfrak m$. The element $c/1$ is nonzero and lies in that maximal ideal (if $c/1$ had inverse $r/s$, then $cr=s$ would contradict $c\in\mathfrak m$ and $s\notin\mathfrak m$). Apply [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] to the local subring $D\subseteq K$. Obtain a valuation ring $V\subseteq K$ containing $D$, whose maximal ideal contracts to that of $D$. Consequently $c/1$ remains nonzero and in the maximal ideal of $V$, so $V$ is not a field. Also $A,B\subseteq C\subseteq D\subseteq V$.

Apply [lem-sc-krull-akizuki-noetherian] with its base ring $R=A$, its fraction field $K$, its finite extension $L=K$ (the identity extension, of degree $1$), and its intermediate ring $D=V$. The ring $A$ is a domain because it is a unital subring of the field $K$; its Noetherian and dimension-one hypotheses are exactly the assumptions of the item. The inclusions $A\subseteq V\subseteq K$ were proved above. Thus $V$ is Noetherian. Step 3 showed that $V$ is a valuation ring and not a field, so [lem-trf-noetherian-valuation-ring-dvr] makes $V$ a DVR. Its fraction field is $K$: the natural fraction subfield of $K$ generated by $V$ contains all $a/b$ with $a,b\in A$, $b\ne0$, hence all of $K$. This supplies the required common DVR.

Conversely suppose $\mathcal O\subseteq K$ is a DVR containing $A$ and $B$. Every finite sum $\sum_i a_i b_i$ lies in $\mathcal O$, so Step 1 gives $\operatorname{im}(\mu)\subseteq\mathcal O$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\mathcal O$ is not a field, and therefore $\mathcal O\ne K$ (the latter is a field). Hence $\operatorname{im}(\mu)\ne K$ and $\mu$ is not surjective. This proves the reverse implication.
